```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is a first paying customer, and only Brief A sources a working consumer price point. Bulletin's live App Store listing shows $3.99/mo, $19.99/yr and $39.99 lifetime, and Ground News's checkout shows $9.99/mo. That is sourced evidence that people pay for this category.",
    "Brief B states outright that no clean payer was found. Every named competitor is free to end users and funded by grants ($930k from Canada's Public Health Agency), VC ($520k for Pointz) or nonprofit dues. Pointz, the one consumer-paid analog, does not publish its price.",
    "Brief A has at least one sourced willingness-to-pay signal: a Syft reviewer wrote 'Revert the UI back and I'll pay.' Brief B's demand quotes show people want the function, but none shows anyone willing to pay for it.",
    "Brief B's credible payers are municipalities, research grants and advocacy nonprofits. These are institutional buyers, and per the brief they already run equivalent free tools. Selling to them inside 90 days is implausible for a solo operator with no relationships.",
    "Brief B also carries a cold-start data-density problem and ongoing liability and moderation burden for safety-critical content. Brief A's MVP is useful to a single user on day one.",
    "Brief A's real risks are saturation, the Artifact shutdown, and free features being absorbed by Apple News, Google News and chatbots. Those threaten long-term scale and retention more than the narrower goal of landing a first paying subscriber."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Brief B's Case For claims 'a credible non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants)' with no source showing any city or agency paying a third-party vendor for this kind of tool. Its own Open Question 1 admits it is unknown whether cities would pay rather than keep their own free forms. The League of American Bicyclists' $50/yr dues are membership fees to the nonprofit, not evidence that anyone pays for a hazard-mapping product.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence on the 90-day criterion. Brief A wins mainly because Brief B has no sourced payer, not because A's demand evidence is strong. A rests on one app-store review and on competitors' price lists, with no conversion, revenue or retention data. Its sustainability case is weakened by the Artifact shutdown and heavy free competition. Neither brief contains direct evidence of a solo builder reaching paid customers."
}
```
